A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 34-page versions of the same LR-QR work, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–O support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original coverage and prediction-set-size evaluations on Communities and Crime, MMLU, and RxRx1, plus regularization ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A–C, including Table 1 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain the same pinball-loss objective, likelihood-ratio regularizer, joint threshold/scalar optimization, and prediction-set construction.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Communities and Crime regression with four demographic shifts, MMLU question answering with educational-level shifts, and RxRx1 image classification across 14 held-out laboratory experiments.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain split conformal, Weighted-CP, 2R-CP, DRO-CP, DR-iso, and Robust-CP. Figure 1 corrects their legend associations without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported data partitions, scoring rules, model configurations, and coverage/set-size metrics are unchanged. Section 5.1 retains the ten-point regularization grid and three-fold cross-validation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 3 retain the same regularization-strength sweep and held-out gradient-norm analysis. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over 1000 random splits for Communities and Crime, 50 for RxRx1, and 100 for the ablations. Error-bar displays and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1 corrects result attribution: blue bars labeled Weighted-CP in v2 are labeled LR-QR in v5, and the other method labels are realigned. The plotted measurements and error bars remain unchanged. Table 1 retains all values, including LR-QR coverage of 89.6% and set size 3.38; Figures 2–4 and written findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, Theorems 4.2–4.3, Corollary 4.4, and the definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices E–O are unchanged. Technical appendix edits concern citation formatting.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims: adapting to covariate shift without directly estimating the likelihood ratio, establishing coverage guarantees through stability analysis, and demonstrating effectiveness on high-dimensional tasks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of regularization, misspecification, overfitting, and extreme regularization strengths are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same qualifications and open questions concerning conditional coverage and regularization selection.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same models, feature construction, likelihood-ratio estimation procedures, tuning details, and implementation link. Added bibliographic metadata does not introduce new implementation or data-access information.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning are unchanged. v5 consolidates the duplicate Gibbs et al. preprint/publication entries under the 2025 publication and consistently swaps the Park 2022a/b labels; these identify the same works.

P1.justification: v5 retitles the paper, standardizes citation and bibliography formatting, and corrects punctuation. Section organization and substantive exposition remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 fixes its shifted legend: the dashed line changes from LR-QR to Nominal Coverage (0.8), and method labels are correctly matched to all seven bar colors. Bibliographic formatting causes minor reflow; the remaining figures and table retain their displays.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 1's misleading legend lets readers identify the methods' results accurately and aligns the figure with Section 5.2's discussion. This is a concrete but limited improvement, accompanied by citation cleanup; the method, theory, experimental scope, and plotted measurements remain unchanged.
